title: VRF affinity rotation causing intermittent tenant hostname mismatch
creator: Maya Chen
description: Multiple Dedicated customers reported intermittent failures resolving internal service hostnames immediately after autoscaler-driven GPU pool reshuffles or peering flaps. Symptoms: tenant A's requests occasionally receive DNS responses that resolve to tenant B's internal hostname (same FQDN path), causing authentication failures and GRPC TLS SNI mismatches. Initial impact surfaced in two high-traffic Dedicated customers and one Private site using peered VPCs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision two tenants in the same region with VPC peering and overlapping overlay VRF ranges (synthetic testbed mirrors customer config).
2) Trigger a scale-down event on one tenant's dedicated GPU pool to force VNI/VRF reassignment and overlay rebalancing.
3) Immediately run repeated DNS lookups for internal service hostnames from tenant workloads while the control plane completes peering reconciliation.
4) Observe intermittent DNS answers pointing at the other tenant's internal service IP (1-2% of queries during the window).
observed_metrics_and_logs: spike in dns_response_mismatch{region="us-west-2"} during scale events (grafana/dedicated-networking dashboard)
conntrack entries with stale VRF tag after vni swap (k8s node logs)
support tickets: #SUP-53219, #SUP-53306 referencing TLS SNI mismatch and 403s
initial_hypothesis: Control-plane reconciliation for VNI/VRF assignments races with dataplane route/prune jobs. During the window, responses from cached resolvers were being sourced from a path still referencing the old VRF mapping, causing cross-tenant name resolution leakage.
root_cause: Race between vpc-controller's VNI reallocation and the egress-route-pruner job. When VNI->VRF bindings were moved, dataplane SNAT/conntrack entries kept stale vrf_id tags for a short window. DNS cache/forwarder (node-resolver) would pick a reply path backed by stale conntrack state, returning an internal IP from the previous tenant VRF. The immediate trigger was an autoscaler-induced pool resize combined with a near-simultaneous peering route update from the control plane.
mitigation_taken: Temporarily increased reconciliation backoff and added fast-validity checks in peering controller to avoid VNI moves during autoscaler cooldown. Rolled an emergency patch to avoid VNI reassignment when active conntrack entries exist and increased DNS TTL jitter to reduce synchronous cache hits. Communication sent to affected customers with status updates and workaround steps.
permanent_fix_plan: 1) Modify r-infra/vpc-controller to perform a two-phase VNI handoff: mark target VRF as draining, wait for conntrack and kv-cache quiesce; then reassign VNI and prune. 2) Add atomic VRF tag update to dataplane so conntrack entries are updated in-place where feasible. 3) Harden resolver to validate that response IP addresses map to the requesting tenant's VRF before returning; if mismatch, trigger a fresh upstream query. 4) Add e2e scenario in CI that simulates VNI/VRF swaps under load.
rollout_plan: - PRs: GH #4876 (vpc-controller two-phase handoff), GH #4893 (dataplane conntrack tag patch), GH #4901 (resolver VRF validation)
deployment_strategy: Canary rollout to a single non-production Dedicated zone first (canary for 24h with synthetic DNS probes), then staged rollouts to low-risk customers, then ramp to all Dedicated and Private clusters. Auto-rollback on alert thresholds (dns_mismatch_rate > 0.1% sustained for 30m).
tests_added: Unit tests for two-phase handoff state transitions
Integration test: simulate VNI reassign under 10k qps DNS traffic and assert zero cross-tenant resolutions
E2E canary job: nightly probe job that triggers autoscaler resize and asserts resolver integrity
references: Support ticket SUP-53219: customer logs and pcap (internal link)
